title: Guser: A GPGPU Power Stressmark Generator
problem: The paper addresses the challenge of systematically generating power stressmarks for GPGPUs to accurately estimate Thermal Design Power (TDP) and enable effective power control. Existing approaches for CPU-based stressmark generation do not effectively translate to GPGPU architectures.
motivation: Accurate power stressmarks are essential for understanding GPU thermal characteristics and designing efficient power management systems.
method: Guser employs three main techniques: (1) Instruction Power Analysis (IPA) characterizes the power consumption of individual PTX instructions, (2) Pipeline-based Instruction Grouping (PIG) classifies instructions into groups with similar power behavior, and (3) Quantifying the Importance of power impact factors (QIF) identifies key adjustable parameters. The system then applies Bayesian Optimization (Optuna) to generate stressmark code that maximizes power consumption on target GPGPU architectures.
key_novelty: First systematic methodology to generate GPGPU power stressmarks through instruction-level power analysis and Bayesian Optimization-guided synthesis.
contributions: First systematic methodology for GPGPU power stressmark generation
Instruction Power Analysis (IPA) technique for characterizing PTX instruction power behavior
Pipeline-based Instruction Grouping (PIG) for classifying instructions by power characteristics
Quantifying power impact factors (QIF) to identify important optimization knobs
primary_theme: GPU power stressmark generation via instruction analysis
